question.problem: When $p(x)=9{x}^{3}+m{x}^{2}+x-2$ is divided by $3x-1$ the remainder is $2.$ What is the value of $m?$
question.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $3x-1=3(x-\frac{1}{3}),$ the remainder equals $p(\frac{1}{3}).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $2,$ then, we must have $p(\frac{1}{3})=2.$

Evaluating $p(\frac{1}{3})$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}p(\frac{1}{3}) & =9{(\frac{1}{3})}^{3}+m{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}-2 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{m}{9}+\frac{1}{3}-2 \\  & =\frac{m}{9}-\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{m-12}{9},\end{aligned}
$$

which means that

$$
2=\frac{m-12}{9}.
$$

Solving for $m$ in the equation above, we find that $m=30.$
